title: Sails Timelock Evaluator 1.0
description: Evaluates whether an explicitly-supplied evaluation time is at or after an explicitly-supplied deadline. Consumes no implicit clock and no external state of any kind — see docs/CORE_ARCHITECTURE.md section 24 (Time) and section 14 (Semantic Binding). This is the semantic definition; a TypeScript reference implementation exists at packages/sails-core/src/evaluators/timelock-evaluator.ts, but that implementation is not itself the definition of this identity — see docs/CORE_IMPLEMENTATION_ARCHITECTURE.md section 19 (Language Neutrality).

inputs.name: deadline
inputs.description: The already-recorded deadline this evaluation checks against — an integer number of milliseconds since the Unix epoch, per the semantic profile's integer/time representation rule. Supplied by the caller; this evaluator never reads or infers it from anywhere else.

inputs.name: evaluationTime
inputs.description: The explicit evaluation time supplied by the calling Runtime for this specific evaluation — never read from an implicit wall clock by the evaluator itself. Two evaluations of the same deadline with different explicit evaluationTime values may legitimately produce different results; this is expected, not nondeterminism, since the input itself differs.

output.rationale: A bare deadline comparison over monotonically-increasing time can always eventually reach SATISFIED and depends on no uncertain input, so UNSATISFIABLE and UNKNOWN are never produced by this specific evaluator. This is a genuine property of this evaluator's own minimal semantics, not an omission — inventing a way to reach all four states here would misrepresent what this evaluator actually does. A richer future evaluator (e.g. one also considering a cancellation Assertion) could legitimately reach all four states under its own, separate identity.

rule: output = SATISFIED if evaluationTime >= deadline, otherwise NOT_YET_SATISFIED. Comparison is standard integer >=, per the semantic profile's integerRepresentation rule — never a strict > , which would incorrectly classify the exact deadline instant itself as not-yet-satisfied.
determinism: Pure function of (deadline, evaluationTime) only. No side effects, no hidden inputs. The same input pair always produces the same output.
normativeReferences: docs/CORE_ARCHITECTURE.md section 12-14 (Condition Semantics, Semantic Binding, UNKNOWN/System-Error Boundary)
